_note: WHAT THIS INSTRUMENT CAN AND CANNOT SEE, recorded with #883 C1 against the #873 ruling in docs/decisions.md ("Performance and Rust byte plane"). Since the Atlas census batched its per-table COUNT(*) calls into one compound SELECT per database file, registering a table costs a SCAN and never a STATEMENT — so a statement count no longer proxies per-table scan cost. These budgets still catch what they were built for: a screen that starts issuing N+1 round trips on first paint. What they can no longer see is growth in the registry, which they used to track by accident; a screen whose scanned bytes double while its statement count holds at 13 reads as unchanged here. The successor instrument for that trend is wall-clock or scanned-table, NOT a re-raised statement count — raising these numbers back would restore the coupling #873 removed rather than restore the signal. Read the same caution wherever a statement count is published as a mechanism witness (for example `vault statements per commit` in tests/scale/replica-sse-fanout.scale.test.ts, which is published beside a wall clock and deliberately not gated).
